R-squared of a Model as Numbers

Source: R/R2_glmm.R
R2_model.Rd

The R-squared of a model as a numeric result, for every model class of predictmeans. method = "piepho" (the default) gives the same values as R2_glmm() of predictmeans 1.x (removed in 2.0; Piepho, 2023), as proportions: total, fixed, random and each random-effect component. method = "nakagawa" gives the marginal (fixed effects) and conditional (fixed and random effects) R-squared of Nakagawa and Schielzeth (2013), with random slopes as Johnson (2014): the variance of each random-effect term is the mean of \(z_i' \Sigma z_i\) over the observations.

Usage

R2_model(model, method = c("piepho", "nakagawa"), over_disp = FALSE)

Arguments

model

A model of any class predictmeans handles: lm, aov (also with Error()), glm, gls, lme, lmer, glmer, glmmTMB, gam or a semireg fit.

method

"piepho" (every class) or "nakagawa" (lmer, glmer, glmmTMB and lme; for lme with a variance or correlation structure the observation-level variance is the mean residual variance).

over_disp

For "piepho" with lmer, glmer and glmmTMB models: TRUE leaves an observation-level random effect (one level per observation, modelling overdispersion) out of the random share; the model must have one. Default FALSE.

Value

A named numeric vector of proportions (class "pm_r2", printed as percentages). For "nakagawa", Marginal and Conditional, with attribute "variances": the fixed-effect, random-effect and observation-level variances. The Nakagawa values agree with performance::r2_nakagawa() (tests/testthat/test-r2-model.R). Notes on the choice of method are kept in attr(, "advice") (advice).

Details

Piepho's R-squared is one definition for every class: the variance of the fixed part of the model (less the bias from estimating the coefficients) and of the random effects, as shares of the average variance of the data. For models without random effects (lm, aov, glm, gls) Total equals Fixed and Random is 0; for lm and aov it is the usual adjusted R-squared. glm models are measured on the link scale (working variances; the latent distribution for a binary response); gls and lme models with any correlation and variance structure; aov models with Error() from the stratum variance components of varcomp. In gam models the smooths are part of the fixed share, except random-effect smooths (bs = "re").

For "nakagawa" the observation-level variance is the residual variance for gaussian models and the variance of the latent distribution for binomial models: \(\pi^2/3\) (logit), 1 (probit) or \(\pi^2/6\) (cloglog). Other families have several competing approximations; use method = "piepho" for them.

References

Piepho, H.-P. (2023), An adjusted coefficient of determination (R2) for generalized linear mixed models in one go, Biometrical Journal, 65(7), 2200290.

Nakagawa, S. and Schielzeth, H. (2013), A general and simple method for obtaining R2 from generalized linear mixed-effects models, Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 4, 133-142.

Johnson, P. C. D. (2014), Extension of Nakagawa & Schielzeth's R2GLMM to random slopes models, Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 5, 944-946.

See also

varcomp, advice

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  fm <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
  R2_model(fm)
#> # Adjusted R2 for mixed models (Piepho)
#>        Total        Fixed       Random      Subject Subject.Days 
#>       79.36%       28.02%       51.34%       18.32%       30.43% 
  R2_model(fm, "nakagawa")
#> # R2 for mixed models (Nakagawa and Schielzeth)
#>    Marginal Conditional 
#>      27.87%      79.92% 
  R2_model(lm(Reaction ~ Days, data = sleepstudy))   # the adjusted R-squared
#> # Adjusted R2 (Piepho)
#>  Total  Fixed Random 
#> 28.25% 28.25%  0.00% 
  R2_model(glm(breaks ~ wool*tension, family = poisson, data = warpbreaks))
#> # Adjusted R2 (Piepho)
#>  Total  Fixed Random 
#> 63.54% 63.54%  0.00% 
#> 
#> Advice:
#> i For a non-gaussian model the R2 is on the link (latent) scale: not
#>   comparable with an lm R2 or across families and links; use it to compare
#>   models of the same family.
